chunks: Muhammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh al-Kūfī narrated from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān al-Nakhaʿī, from his uncle al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Sālim, from his father, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said to him: How did the inheritance come to be
for the male is the like of the share of two females
So he said: Because the grains that Ādam عليه السلام and Ḥawwāʾ ate in Paradise were eighteen grains. Ādam ate twelve grains of them, and Ḥawwāʾ ate six. Therefore the inheritance came to be
for the male is the like of the share of two females

key_terms.الْحَبَّاتِ: the grains mentioned as having been eaten in Paradise
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: inheritance; the division of an estate among heirs
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: the legal inheritance formula that the male receives the share of two females

ai.seo_question: Why is the male's inheritance share equal to that of two females in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a transmitted explanation for the inheritance rule expressed as: for the male is the share of two females. It connects that ruling to the account of Ādam عليه السلام and Ḥawwāʾ in Paradise, framing the legal ratio through a narrative cause mentioned by Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام.
